styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Independence Hall, the Liberty Bell and Old City's colonial streets.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Cheesesteaks, Reading Terminal Market and neighborhood BYOBs.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: The Barnes, the Museum of Art steps and murals all over town.

stays.why: Most central. Walk to City Hall, Reading Terminal Market and the subway; short walk or ride to Old City.
Steps from Independence Hall, the Liberty Bell and Elfreth's Alley. Quieter at night.
Leafy, upscale and full of restaurants and shops. Good base for food and shopping.
Near Penn, Drexel and the museums along the Schuylkill. Cheaper rooms, short ride to Center City.

food: Order a cheesesteak at a classic stand; ask for 'wit' or 'witout' onions. Expect about $10–15.
Reading Terminal Market: one big hall of local food stalls. Go hungry and early; it is busy at lunch.
Try a soft pretzel and water ice (Italian ice) — two cheap Philadelphia classics.
Many small restaurants are BYOB; bring your own wine and save on the bill.
Book ahead for popular dinner spots on weekends. Prices range from cheap eats to fine dining.
more_time: Add a day for the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Rocky Steps, then walk the Schuylkill River Trail.
Eastern State Penitentiary and the Barnes Foundation make a good half-day in Fairmount.
In summer, take the RiverLink ferry to Camden for the waterfront and aquarium.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Independence Hall, the museums and a proper food crawl; add a night for Fairmount and the river.

month_notes: Cold: highs near 5°C, lows below freezing. Pack a warm coat and gloves.
Still cold, highs around 8°C. Indoor sights are the safe bet.
Mild and changeable, highs near 12°C. Bring a rain jacket.
Spring warms up to about 17°C. Good walking weather; expect some rain.
Pleasant, highs around 23°C. One of the best months to be outside.
Warm at about 28°C. Comfortable mornings; watch for afternoon showers.
Hottest month, highs near 31°C and humid. Plan indoor breaks midday.
Hot and humid, similar to July. Carry water and go slow.
Warm and pleasant again at about 26°C. Great for parks and walking.
Crisp fall days around 20°C. Good for sightseeing; fewer rain days.
Cooler at about 13°C. Layer up; rain is less likely.
Cold again, highs near 8°C. Holiday lights make evenings cheerful.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold winters, warm humid summers, and the best weather in spring and fall.

items.title: Best time: April to June and September to October
items.text: Highs around 17–26°C with moderate rain. Ideal for walking Old City and the parks.

items.title: Summer is hot and humid (July–August)
items.text: Highs near 30–31°C. Plan indoor sights at midday and carry water.

items.title: Winter is cold (December–February)
items.text: Highs around 5–8°C and lows near or below freezing. Bring a warm coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 8–14 rain days a month, most in July. A small umbrella is worth packing any month.

items.title: Fall is crisp and clear
items.text: October and November are cooler with fewer rain days — good for long walks.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers and comfortable walking shoes. Add a rain jacket, and a heavy coat for winter visits.

transit.best: Walk in Center City and use SEPTA for longer hops; ride apps for late nights.

modes.text: SEPTA runs the subway and trolleys; fares are about $2–2.50 per ride. Pay with a SEPTA Key card or contactless.
Buses cover the whole city. SEPTA Key card or contactless payment works.
Taxis are metered. Uber and Lyft both operate widely.
Driving is possible but parking is costly and traffic is heavy in Center City.
Easy in Center City; most sights are within 30 minutes on foot.
Bikes are popular; the Schuylkill River Trail is a favorite.
The RiverLink ferry runs to Camden in summer.
